hints: Point B is reached when the sledge first comes to rest, so find where the velocity line first meets v = 0.
walkthrough: The sledge travels from A to B while its velocity is positive.
At B it comes to rest, which is the first point where the velocity–time line reaches v = 0.
Reading the time coordinate of that intercept gives 12 s.

ai_rubric.observable: Reads the first zero-velocity intercept as a travel time of 12 s.

hints: Find displacement from the signed area under the velocity–time graph.
Split the graph at t = 12 s, where the sledge is at rest: one triangle lies above the axis and one lies below it.
Use the magnitude of each triangular area, then subtract the below-axis area because that motion is back towards A.
walkthrough: Displacement is the signed area under a velocity–time graph.
From t = 0 to 12 s, the area above the axis is a triangle: ½ × 12 × 18 = 108 m up the slope from A.
From t = 12 s to 24 s, the area below the axis has magnitude ½ × 12 × 6 = 36 m and represents motion back towards A.
The displacement from A at 24 s is 108 − 36 = 72 m up the slope.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds the 0–12 s displacement from the positive triangular graph area as 108 m.
Finds the 12–24 s displacement magnitude from the negative triangular graph area as 36 m.
Uses signed displacement to obtain 72 m up the slope from A at 24 s.

hints: Use the straight section of the velocity–time graph after the sledge leaves B, where the velocity changes uniformly.
Take the gradient of that section using its endpoints: velocity changes from 0 to −6 m s⁻¹ between 12 s and 24 s.
The negative sign indicates the direction towards A; report the acceleration magnitude in that stated direction.
walkthrough: From B to A, the velocity–time graph is a straight line, so the acceleration is its gradient.
Taking up the slope as positive, the velocity changes from 0 m s⁻¹ at 12 s to −6 m s⁻¹ at 24 s.
The negative sign means the acceleration is down the slope towards A, so its magnitude is 0.50 m s⁻². Equivalent constant-acceleration equations using the graph areas give the same result.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the velocity–time gradient or a valid constant-acceleration relationship for the B-to-A motion.
Evaluates a valid route using the graph data to obtain an acceleration magnitude of 0.50 m s⁻² towards A.

hints: Consider forces along the slope while the sledge accelerates from B towards A.
Use the 70 kg mass and 0.50 m s⁻² acceleration to find the resultant downslope force.
The 80 N weight component acts downslope; friction acts up the slope, so compare it with the resultant force.
walkthrough: Take down the slope towards A as positive. The sledge accelerates at 0.50 m s⁻², so the resultant force is F = ma = 70 × 0.50 = 35 N downslope.
The component of weight is 80 N downslope and friction acts upslope.
Therefore 80 − friction = 35, giving friction = 45 N.
The frictional force is 45 N up the slope, opposing the motion.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses F = ma to obtain a resultant force of 35 N down the slope.
Balances the 80 N downslope weight component with the resultant force to obtain a frictional force of 45 N opposing the motion.

hints: The stated 80 N force is the component of the total weight parallel to the slope.
Calculate the total weight from the 70 kg mass, then relate its downslope component to the slope angle.
Use 80 = (70 × 9.81) sin θ and take the inverse sine.
walkthrough: The total weight of the child and sledge is W = mg = 70 × 9.81 N.
For a slope at angle θ to the horizontal, the component of weight down the slope is W sin θ.
Therefore 80 = (70 × 9.81) sin θ, so sin θ = 80 / (70 × 9.81).

ai_rubric.observable: Relates the 80 N downslope weight component to the total weight using sin θ = 80 / (70 × 9.81).

hints: The initial whistle sound is emitted at t = 4.0 s, so read the sledge speed from the velocity–time graph at that time.
At t = 4.0 s the sledge is moving away from the man at A, so choose the moving-source Doppler form with v + vₛ in the denominator.
Substitute fₛ = 900 Hz, v = 340 m s⁻¹ and the graph speed into fₒ = fₛv / (v + vₛ).
walkthrough: At t = 4.0 s, Fig. 3.2 gives the sledge speed as 12 m s⁻¹. It is moving away from the man at A.
For a source moving away from a stationary observer, use fₒ = fₛv / (v + vₛ).
The initial observed frequency is 870 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Reads a source speed of 12 m s⁻¹ at t = 4.0 s and uses the moving-away Doppler relationship with fₛ = 900 Hz and v = 340 m s⁻¹.
Calculates the initial observed frequency as 870 Hz.

hints: From t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s, compare the sledge speed on the graph while it continues to move away from A.
walkthrough: The sledge is moving away from the man while the whistle sounds, but its speed decreases between t = 4.0 s and t = 8.0 s.
A smaller recession speed produces a smaller Doppler shift.
Therefore the frequency heard by the man increases, moving closer to the emitted 900 Hz frequency.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that the sledge speed decreases while it moves away from the man, so the observed frequency increases.
